title: Quantinuum and RIKEN Execute End-to-End Hybrid Quantum-HPC Chemistry on Fugaku and Reimei - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Quantinuum and RIKEN ran an end-to-end hybrid quantum-HPC chemistry workflow coupling 96 Fugaku nodes with the on-premises 20-qubit Reimei trapped-ion machine via direct-access APIs, using an ONIOM partition and TE-QSCI on 16 error-detected logical qubits. The quantum step cut excitation-energy error versus the classical baseline from 0.18 eV to 0.03 eV against full CASCI(8,8) for retinal in a carbon nanotube.

insights.claim: Quantinuum and RIKEN linked 96 A64FX nodes of Japan's Fugaku supercomputer with Quantinuum's on-premises Reimei trapped-ion processor (20 physical qubits) in a single orchestrated quantum-classical chemistry workflow.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: On-prem quantum coprocessors co-located at national HPC centers are moving from announcements to working integrated workloads — a datapoint for Quantinuum's HPC-integration go-to-market.

insights.claim: The Fugaku-Reimei workflow was orchestrated with Quantinuum's Tierkreis dataflow framework and TKET compilation, managing asynchronous scheduling between Fugaku's workload manager and Reimei's direct-access API.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantinuum's software stack (Tierkreis/TKET) is serving as the glue layer for HPC integration, a potential lock-in point beyond hardware.

insights.claim: Replacing cloud-based multi-tenant job queues with direct API orchestration lets a quantum processor be scheduled as a coprocessor inside an active national supercomputing center.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals a deployment model (dedicated on-prem QPU with direct API) competing with cloud-access quantum business models.

insights.claim: The project was commissioned under Japan's New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO) initiative.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Japanese government funding is underwriting quantum-HPC integration, supporting demand for vendors embedded in Japan's national labs.

insights.claim: The workflow uses subtractive ONIOM (QM1/QM2) partitioning so classical HPC handles the large weakly correlated environment (carbon nanotube wall) while the quantum processor handles the strongly correlated active site (retinal).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Embedding schemes that confine quantum resources to small active sites are the practical path to near-term chemistry value with few logical qubits.

insights.claim: Fugaku ran geometry optimization, Hartree-Fock and configuration interaction singles via the NTChem suite, then diagonalized the subspace Hamiltonian from configurations sampled on the quantum machine.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Classical HPC remains the bulk of the compute; quantum acts as a sampler, so HPC centers stay central in hybrid value chains.

insights.claim: Time-Evolved Quantum Selected CI (TE-QSCI) initializes an approximate complete active space wavefunction on 16 logical qubits and samples Krylov-subspace configurations under Trotterized time evolution, rather than relying on a single-reference ansatz.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sample-based quantum diagonalization methods are emerging as the leading near-term chemistry algorithms to watch.
insights.locator: To compute the strongly correlated active site

insights.claim: Logical circuits on Reimei were protected by an [[18,16,2]] 'iceberg' error-detection code with post-selection, achieving a 67.9% average survival rate across 12,214 shots.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A ~32% discard rate quantifies the current overhead cost of error detection on 16 logical qubits.

insights.claim: TE-QSCI found 2,149 new electronic configurations outside the initial classical active space and captured the leading six configurations of the full CASCI(8,8) reference.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Evidence the quantum sampler adds information beyond the classical baseline rather than merely reproducing it.

insights.claim: The hybrid calculation reached eigenstate fidelities of 0.994 (S0), 0.995 (S1) and 0.996 (T0), reducing excitation-energy error versus the classical baseline from 0.18 eV to 0.03 eV relative to full CASCI(8,8).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 6x error reduction at a chemically relevant scale is a concrete benchmark for quantum chemistry claims — though the reference is still classically computable (CASCI(8,8)).
